newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission probes 24 mln Ecus aid to Dutch Oce.
newsitem.headline: Commission probes 24 mln Ecus aid to Dutch Oce.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was investigating 24 million Ecus aid paid or promised to Dutch photocopier and printer maker Oce Nederland BV to help it develop a digital high-volume copier.
The Commission said it had doubts about 12 million Ecus granted in 1994 with its permission which might be excessive in the light of recent information regarding the cost of the project.

"Aid to Oce in 1994 was approved by the Commission partly on the basis that the Ecu 12 million in the form of a repayable advance represented about 10 percent of the eligible project costs, which were understood at the time to be Ecu 108 million", it said in statement IP/96/1048.
But the 108-million-Ecu figure represented the total costs and not all are eligible for subsidies under EU rules on aid to research, the Commission said.

The Commisssion also said it had "serious doubts" about another 12 million Ecus promised by the Dutch government to Oce, again in the form of a repayable advance, saying that the company was likely to have carried out the project with or without state money.
"The 'incentive' effect of the proposed aid - an inducement for the company to carry out research which it would not otherwise have pursued - is doubtful", the statement said.
